採用・広告の製品.quote: Turn CAD files into accurate quotes in minutes. A system that standardizes your costing, protects your margins, and keeps running when your best estimator is out of the office.
Hours spent per quote when an estimator has to open files, calculate manually, and build a price from scratch
Person your entire pricing operation depends on when your senior estimator is the system

Every hour spent on manual estimation is an hour not spent on production. Every quote that takes three days is a customer who might not wait. And every business that runs on one person's knowledge is one resignation away from a serious problem.
Quotes take hours or days to prepare
Pricing depends on who picks up the job
When they leave, so does the pricing logic
Drop in a STEP, DXF, DWG, DSTV, NC1 or any of 30+ supported formats. Sheet metal parts, tube profiles, structural sections, full assemblies. Analysis starts immediately.
Built For Your Process
Quotation Factory is not a generic tool adapted for metal. Every calculation, every production route, every material match is built around the specific processes your team runs every day.
Consistent pricing across jobs
Tube, Profile & Structural Steel
The same price, every time
Two estimators, one part, one price. Standardized costing logic means consistent output regardless of who is working.
Your entire quoting operation in one place. CAD analysis, cost calculation, production routing, RFQ management and pricing logic all connected and running automatically.
The quote data flows directly into your ERP as a manufacturing BOM and into your CAM software as machine instructions. Zero manual re-entry between quoting and production.
Where we are today exceeded our expectations completely, but we continue improving workflows, automation, and operational efficiency step by step every single day.
Quotation Factory has helped us speed up our production process and make fewer mistakes.
CEO, Polder Staalproducties

CEO Wim Dijkgraaf had been experimenting with AI around leads and sales conversations. He could see the opportunity. But a company does not become AI-first if every useful idea still has to pass through the founder.

Sales, customer success, marketing and finance needed more than access to another tool. They needed the confidence to describe their own processes, connect the right information and build something repeatable.
Bosar introduced the team to AI First Academy. Each employee received their own training account, with a practical path into Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the AI-first framework.

After completing the training, Quotation Factory formed an internal AI-first project team. Employees started building skills and agents for their own responsibilities, with weekly meetings to keep the work moving.
The starting point was ordinary work: a CRM update, a customer handover, a billing check, a product announcement. Each department built around the information and decisions it already understood.

A rep finished a demo, reopened their notes, updated the CRM and wrote a follow-up from scratch. Preparing a software proposal meant finding the right product information and checking earlier conversations.

A reusable Claude skill brings the call notes together with the account record and approved product information. It prepares the CRM update, outlines the customer’s requirements and drafts a follow-up with a clear next step. The rep checks it, adds their judgment and sends it.
Call notes + account history + product context
CRM update, follow-up and proposal outline
The rep confirms scope, pricing and the message.

A handover arrived as a mix of messages, spreadsheets and sales notes. Customer success pieced together the manufacturer’s process, outstanding questions and onboarding requirements before every call.

Claude reads the agreed handover materials and prepares a customer brief: what the manufacturer wants to improve, what data is still missing and what the next session needs to cover. After the call, the same workflow updates the action list and prepares the customer recap.
Sales handover + onboarding files + meeting notes
An exception list, instead of another spreadsheet pass.

A finance workflow compares the supplied account and billing exports, groups the discrepancies and prepares an exception list with links back to the source rows. Claude drafts the questions and follow-ups; finance reviews the amounts and approves every accounting action.
Approved terms + account export + invoice export
Finance approves invoices, changes and reminders.
One product update. A coherent set of communications.
Turning a release into a customer email, a LinkedIn post and a sales talking point meant starting three times. The product detail lived with developers and the tone depended on who had time to write.

Marketing gives Claude the release notes, approved positioning and a defined audience. A shared skill prepares the email, post and sales summary together, using the same facts and language. The team checks the claims and edits the message before anything goes out.
Marketing checks accuracy and publishes.

Product knowledge, customer definitions, tone of voice and operating rules give Claude a consistent foundation. Department skills then specify the task: what to read, what to produce and what must stay with a person.
Reviewed and approved by the person responsible.
The same structure supports sales, customer success, finance and marketing without removing their judgment.

That distinction matters. Preparing an invoice review is different from approving a financial change. Drafting a sales message is different from making a promise to a customer. The workflow carries the preparation; the team owns the decision.
